I can't open the pic mobile, but I believe I know what this image is. When I first saw it, I was like, how did they take that pic? I was told later that it was stitched together from other pics.

There is an app for the HTC Vive called destinations. It is set up so that you can walk around areas that have been rebuilt from pictures into a 3D environment through photogrammetry, the same technique used to produce this image, I believe.

The Curiosity site is one of those areas that comes with the app. I can tell you, that while there are a lot of cool things about VR, this location was one of the most awesome and disturbing experiences I've had with it.

It was amazing yet terrifying standing there. In my head, I know I'm not on Mars, but I will say, it took me a moment to dial in the fact that I was NOT alone on Mars. I had to slow down my breathing and almost instinctual panic at the experience.

You can walk up to the rover and see it in exquisite detail, as well as move around an area about the size of a football field. All the little landmarks it has encountered there has a pop-up plaque explaining what it is like you would see at a museum.

I stayed up and watched the live-stream of the curiosity landing. This whole endeavor is absolutely amazing. Being able to experience it in VR was just the icing on the cake.
